articles.title: The Articular Dislocation Angle of the First Metatarsophalangeal Joint: Its Conception, Measurement Method, and Role in Hallux Valgus.
articles.authors: Guo M, Liu F, Gan Y, Yang F
articles.study_type: Diagnostic study introducing a new measurement method
articles.population: Patients with hallux valgus (bunions); mean age 58 years, mostly female and Asian
articles.outcomes: Articular dislocation angle (ADA) measurement accurately quantifies joint subluxation; ADA contribution increases with disease severity (43.3% mild to 69.3% severe); weight-bearing radiographs underestimated DASA measurements compared to CT scans
articles.take_home: A new measurement called the articular dislocation angle can accurately measure how much the big toe joint is dislocated in bunions, and this dislocation becomes more significant as the bunion worsens. The formula HVA = DMAA + DASA + ADA helps surgeons understand which parts of the bunion need fixing during surgery.

articles.title: A novel matrix-preserving technique (QS-PFE) versus the winograd procedure for Heifetz stage 3 hallux onychocryptosis in adolescents: A retrospective comparative study.
articles.authors: Unat B, Isik M, Bilgin MA, Karabulut C, Erol R, Kisi I, et al.
articles.population: Adolescents with severe ingrowing toenail (Heifetz stage 3)
articles.sample_size: 325 adolescents (127 in QS-PFE group, 198 in Winograd group)
articles.outcomes: Pain levels (VAS score), recurrence rates, nail-width preservation, return to school and sports, patient satisfaction
articles.take_home: The new QS-PFE technique had higher pain in the first week but much lower pain at 3 and 6 months compared to standard Winograd surgery. It also had significantly fewer cases of the problem returning (less than 1% versus 15%) and higher patient satisfaction (96% versus 68%).

articles.title: First tarsometatarsal joint medial subluxation after contemporary minimally invasive distal osteotomy for hallux valgus: A weight-bearing computed tomography assessment.
articles.authors: Palma J, DiGiovanni G, El Masry S, Zeng A, Thompson R, Jones A, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing minimally invasive surgery for hallux valgus (bunions)
articles.outcomes: First tarsometatarsal joint subluxation measured by a novel imaging parameter (C1-M1 joint lateral distance); midshaft foot width; dorsal displacement
articles.take_home: Minimally invasive bunion surgery consistently caused a small shift in the joint at the base of the big toe (average increase of 1.07 mm) and was associated with increased foot width at the middle of the foot. The clinical significance of these changes is not yet known.

articles.title: Changes in foot and ankle offset between minimally invasive distal first metatarsal osteotomy and modified Lapidus procedures in hallux valgus.
articles.authors: Lama JE, Garibaldi R, Voellmicke I, Lan R, Steineman B, Ellis SJ, et al.
articles.population: Patients with hallux valgus (bunions) treated with surgery
articles.outcomes: Hindfoot alignment measured by Foot and Ankle Offset, calcaneus offset, and hindfoot angle on weight-bearing CT scans
articles.take_home: The Lapidus procedure produced larger changes in hindfoot alignment than distal first metatarsal osteotomy, but neither operation made clinically meaningful improvements to hindfoot positioning.

articles.title: High frequency of secondary surgery after operatively treated talar fractures: A nationwide register study from 2000 to 2022.
articles.authors: Brushtein E, Partio N, Maenpaa H, Mattila VM
articles.population: Adults treated operatively for talar fractures
articles.sample_size: 985 patients (747 early index procedure, 238 delayed index procedure)
articles.outcomes: Frequency of secondary surgical procedures after operatively treated talar fractures
articles.take_home: Nearly one-quarter of patients who had surgery for broken ankle bones (talus) needed at least one further operation. Talar fractures that are treated with surgery carry a substantial risk of needing additional surgery.

articles.title: Comparison of efficiency and cost of anterior ankle arthroscopy performed with needle versus standard arthroscope.
articles.authors: Burnikel AP, Goodloe JB, Hoch C, Cutrone J, Gross CE, Scott DJ
articles.study_type: Prospective cohort study with cost analysis
articles.outcomes: Operating room turnover time, time from incision to joint space, total arthroscopic time, and procedure costs
articles.take_home: Needle arthroscopy was faster than standard arthroscopy, taking about 7 minutes less for the whole procedure and reaching the joint space about 1 minute quicker. There was no significant difference in total costs between the two methods.

articles.title: Additional surgical procedures in total ankle arthroplasty: Narrative review and proposed treatment algorithm.
articles.authors: Morales-Perez E, Herrera-Rodriguez A, Rendon-Diaz D, Ojeda-Jimenez J, Gonzalez-Martin D, Valderrabano V, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing total ankle arthroplasty with coronal deformity
articles.outcomes: Treatment sequence and timing of additional surgical procedures during total ankle arthroplasty; restoration of ankle axis alignment
articles.take_home: When replacing an ankle joint, correcting the angle of the ankle and treating associated problems in the right order is important to help the artificial joint last longer. This review summarises which extra procedures are commonly needed and proposes the best order to perform them.
